body.statement: For every \(P\in\mathrm{Base}_\kappa\), sharp assignment and consistency give \(g_{t,P}=m_{t,P}\) on the restricted support in \(A_t\). The mass condition places every \(x\in B\) in the closure of both supports, so the Lipschitz representatives have unique side limits. Hence \(\theta_{t,P}(x)=\lim_{z\to x,z\in A_t}E_{P^{\mathrm{obs}}}[Y\mid X=z,T=t]\), and \(\tau_P(x)=m_{1,P}(x)-m_{0,P}(x)\) is identified on \(B\).
body.justification: The statistical target is an observed-law functional with a causal interpretation.
body.gap: Published boundary-curve identification is stated under positive density; this lemma allows polynomially vanishing side mass.
body.consumer: Boundary-discontinuity analysts can interpret oracle risk as error for the boundary average treatment-effect curve.
